requirements.requirement: Start the requested number of short jobs, with even-numbered jobs exiting 0 and odd-numbered jobs exiting 3.
requirements.summary: A six-job run produced exactly jobs 0–5 with statuses 0,3,0,3,0,3; a post-restart four-job run repeated the expected pattern.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supervisor running until its children finish and reap every child.
requirements.summary: The supervisor was observed alive after launch, completed successfully, and left no children associated with its PID. Its installed implementation explicitly waits for every child with waitpid before writing results and exiting.

requirements.requirement: Record every job's exit status in results.tsv while preserving previous results.
requirements.summary: The original header and previous,0,0 row remained intact, all six requested job records were appended, and the data persisted across restart. Four additional post-restart records were also appended correctly.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution and restart. The repair uses the already-installed /usr/bin/python interpreter, with no package change evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and system services, persisted results, and supervisor behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot transition and unchanged platform.
limitations: The post-run PPID check occurred after the supervisor exited, so by itself it cannot distinguish supervisor reaping from later orphan adoption; confidence remains high because the waitpid implementation and complete per-job result production coherently support correct reaping behavior.
Lifecycle temporary-file collection is bounded to /tmp; it directly identifies the retained repair file and bytecode cache but is not a full filesystem residue audit.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated system mutation was identified. The supervisor replacement and validation run directly supported the task, while the reboot and post-restart run supported the mandatory restart protocol. The only hygiene defect is minor retained build residue from cmd-b210d47227d34331: /tmp/supervisor.py.repaired and its generated /tmp/__pycache__ content remained after execution instead of being cleaned up. No failed services, new network exposure, or package-health damage was observed.
